title: Regression Hedging, DV01 and PCA

maps.tested: Reported as a numerical in multiple sittings. The sheet notes that the same formula yields both the beta and the face value, so one setup serves two question forms.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'hedge ratio given beta, alpha, DV01'; 'regression hedge: face amount if offsetting'; 'DV01 hedging'; 'regression-based hedge'. LO 11.a, the drawbacks of a plain DV01-neutral hedge, is the qualitative counterpart and the reason the regression hedge exists. PCA as a hedging-portfolio construction (LO 11.h) is the adjacent item.

vardeezReading: MR-11: Important. "Regression Hedge calculation (using the same formula, Beta as well as face value can be calculated)."

selectors.name: Hedge ratio from regression output
selectors.what: From a regression of the yield change of the bond being hedged on the yield change of the hedging bond, pick out beta and the two DV01s and form the hedge ratio beta x DV01 of the hedged bond / DV01 of the hedging bond; alpha is reported but is the tempting extra input that does not belong. The same relation can be solved for beta.
selectors.theory: Why beta, not alpha, enters the hedge: beta is the expected yield change of the hedged bond per unit yield change of the hedging bond and scales the DV01-neutral ratio; the intercept does not enter the face amount. Risk weight (DV01 of the hedge as a fraction of the DV01 of the hedged bonds) equals beta, against 100% for a DV01-neutral hedge.

selectors.name: Regression hedge face amount, P&L volatility
selectors.what: Face amount of the offsetting position F_H = -F_P x (DV01_P / DV01_H) x beta, paired with the hedged P&L volatility = |F_P x DV01_P / 100| x regression standard error (DV01 of the hedged position times the standard error).
selectors.theory: The face amount is the DV01-neutral amount scaled by beta, so with beta below 1 fewer hedging bonds are sold. The P&L volatility uses the DV01 of the position being hedged, not of the hedge leg (using the hedge leg gives beta times the right answer), and the residual risk is the regression standard error.

selectors.name: Trap: DV01-neutral amount as distractor
selectors.what: DV01 hedging: the DV01-neutral face amount F_H = -F_P x DV01_P / DV01_H (risk weight 100%) sits among the options against the regression amount, which is smaller by the factor beta; dropping beta is the planted error.
selectors.theory: The DV01-neutral hedge is the regression hedge with beta set to one, that is, it assumes parallel yield shifts; the regression hedge scales it by the estimated beta.

selectors.name: Drawbacks of DV01-neutral hedge
selectors.what: Qualitative: a DV01-neutral hedge assumes the yields of the hedged and hedging bonds move in parallel, which is questionable when the corporate bond trades at a changing spread and the two rates are not perfectly correlated; the regression hedge, with least-squares beta, minimises the variance of the hedged P&L.

selectors.name: PCA hedging portfolio, risk-weight sum
selectors.what: PCA as the construction of a hedging portfolio: shift the curve by each principal component, reprice, compute a '01 per component and choose hedges that neutralise them. With two hedging securities only two PCs (level and slope) can be neutralised, and the PCA risk weights need not sum to 100%; only parallel-shift hedges do.

notSelected: MR-11 e (two-variable regression hedge), MR-11 f (level versus change regressions) and MR-11 g (reverse regression) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer, and MR-11 h is selected only as the construction of a hedging portfolio, not the properties of PCA (variance shares, uncorrelated components, level, slope and short-rate shapes) in general.
